name: Tiroler Steinöl Vitalberg Pertisau
kurzbeschreibung: The Vitalberg Tyrolean Shale Oil Museum in Pertisau on Lake Achensee: futuristic glass mountain showcasing the history of Alpine 'Black Gold' since 1902.
beschreibung:
Overview

The spectacular discovery museum Vitalberg – Tiroler Steinöl Museum is situated in the heart of the picturesque holiday resort of Pertisau directly on the western shore of the Achensee at an altitude of around 940 metres. From the outside, the museum immediately catches every eye: the building was designed in the shape of a futuristic, faceted mountain peak constructed from shimmering green glass and steel. Opened in 2003, the venue is dedicated to Tiroler Steinöl – the legendary "Black Gold of Lake Achensee" –, which has been extracted from fossil-bearing oil shale in the neighbouring Karwendelgebirge for over a century and is treasured worldwide for its natural healing and skincare benefits.

Route & Requirements

The discovery of Tyrolean stone oil traces back to the pioneering mining figure Martin Albrecht: in 1902, he uncovered rich deposits of fossilized oil shale (ichthyol rock) in the remote Bächental valley in the Karwendel mountains at over 1,500 metres above sea level. Heating the 180-million-year-old rock to over 450 °C releases the sulfur-rich organic oil – fossilized organic remains of ancient marine creatures from the prehistoric Tethys Ocean. In the underground exhibition area of the Vitalberg, visitors walk through an authentically reconstructed mining gallery. Multimedia exhibits, historical film footage, and original tools vividly illustrate the hardships endured by high-mountain miners and the refined distillation of crude shale oil into therapeutic ointments, shampoos, and massage balms. The circuit offers profound insight into the medicinal effects of sulfur in relieving joint conditions, rheumatism, and skin disorders. The architectural crown is the glass summit pyramid, which houses a stylish panoramic café featuring a sun terrace with sweeping views across the Karwendelgebirge and the glistening waters of the Achensee.

Visit & Arrival

The Vitalberg discovery museum and café are open daily during the summer season from early May to late October from 09:00 to 18:00 (in winter from mid-December to Easter daily from 10:00 to 17:00). Museum admission prices (2025/2026 season): adults approx. €7.50, seniors approx. €6.50, children (6 to 15 years) approx. €4.00, young children free; family ticket approx. €16.00. Holders of the regional Achensee Erlebniscard enjoy free admission! The ground-floor shop in the foyer can be visited freely without an admission ticket. Arrival by car: Via the Inntal autobahn A12 (exit Wiesing/Achensee), along the Achenseebundesstraße B181 towards Maurach and continuing to Pertisau directly to the Vitalberg along the lakeside promenade (parking available at the Karwendelbahn lift or the lakeside promenade). By public transport: ÖBB trains to Jenbach railway station, from where bus line 4080 runs directly to the Pertisau Information bus stop (just a two-minute walk away).

Tips

The entire Vitalberg museum, all exhibition areas, and the upper-level panorama café are completely barrier-free and wheelchair-accessible thanks to a modern passenger elevator. In the connected factory boutique, staff provide expert guidance and visitors can sample the popular shale oil bath remedies and skincare tonics before purchasing. Enjoy a cappuccino on the panoramic terrace while watching the historic Achensee steamships glide across the lake.
